claims.statement: The reusable `_test.yml` workflow validates required JSON matrix inputs before expanding a non-fail-fast build matrix, then checks out code, uses the local uv setup action, synchronizes the test group, runs platform-specific unit-test commands, and verifies a clean working tree.

`_test.yml` reads maintainer bypass labels from the live GitHub API only for pull-request runs and fails closed if that lookup fails; `ci:allow-warnings` adds `-W default`, while the narrowly scoped release ripgrep bypass can tolerate an install failure and record an artifact without weakening push or merge-group enforcement.

The ripgrep installer uses a pinned ripgrep 14.1.0 Linux x86_64 musl archive, verifies its SHA-256 before installing `rg`, and exits nonzero for unsupported architecture or installation failures so workflow callers retain policy control.

`ripgrep_timeout_comment.yml` consumes completed PR CI runs without checking out PR code, uses artifact names and a head-SHA stale-run guard to manage a bot-owned sticky warning, and treats an unresolvable PR as a logged race rather than a failing comment job.

The ripgrep warning workflow distinguishes a bypassed release-PR install failure from an ordinary PR timeout by PR kind, while a failed live-label read only leaves release dispatch propagation unconfirmed; marker artifacts identify legs that lost ripgrep coverage rather than proving that coverage passed.

Workflow contract tests execute ripgrep install and bypass branches with stubbed commands, enforce release-predicate and reporting alignment, and separately verify that CI matrices follow package `requires-python` policy and that credentials remain scoped to their intended workflow or step.

`sync_priority_labels.yml` derives priority from closing links in PR bodies, propagates only `priority:urgent` or `priority:high` from the highest-priority linked issue, and removes backlog and retired priority labels from PRs.
The priority synchronizer uses `pull_request_target` without checking out PR code, scopes concurrent work by PR, issue, or backfill, and gives label-writing permissions only to its mutation jobs.
The reusable Harbor worker supports either a caller-provided flat matrix or single-dataset shard expansion, derives an effective parallel pool, and runs a non-fail-fast Harbor matrix.

Harbor limits the secret-bearing leaf job to read-only GitHub token permissions while its aggregate job alone receives `actions: write` to download and clean up shard artifacts; aggregation runs after non-cancelled work and reports over available shards without failing the paid evaluation workflow.

The Harbor credential check conditionally injects provider keys by model/category and rejects unsupported providers, sandbox types, malformed OpenRouter judge slugs, and missing required credentials before evaluation execution.

Unified evaluations call the Harbor reusable workflow once per prepared model matrix, isolate LangSmith cost querying to a best-effort usage job in the `evals` environment, and keep that API key out of the write-capable result-combine job.

Release-please rejects empty commits and malformed or unmatched release detection before dispatch, and its dispatch job reads merged release-PR labels fail-closed before propagating the two dangerous bypass inputs.

The release build validates normal release SHA ancestry and package version at that SHA, while its pre-release checks fan out across the resolved Python matrix with read-only permissions and no cache.

Release ripgrep checks fail installation unless the explicit dangerous input is true, preserve coverage if an `rg` probe succeeds, and otherwise record that artifact tests ran without ripgrep coverage before allowing gated tests to skip.

Static tests execute release target SHA resolution with a temporary repository and stubbed GitHub CLI, covering deterministic merged-PR summary selection, lookup/parse failures, and dangerous release ancestry validation.

Credential-scoping tests lock down App-token references, package-conditional integration secrets, disabled release integration wiring, dedicated OpenWiki token sequencing, and step-only topic-classifier secrets.

`ci.yml` selects reusable package test jobs from path filters on pull requests and merge-group runs, runs every package job on pushes to `main`, and its warnings contract test requires every discovered package under `libs/` to be wired to `_test.yml`.

The `✅ CI Success` gate runs trusted base-ref gate logic, always requires lockfile validation, keeps push and merge-group evaluation strict, and permits only failed Talon jobs on qualifying non-Talon-source pull requests to be waived with advisory reporting.

Warnings-as-errors contract tests execute the live label-resolution shell step with a stubbed GitHub CLI, verify exact label matching and API-error fail-closed behavior, and require both platform-specific test commands to consume the resolved warning flag.

Curated release-note automation validates target events before privileged work, executes helper code from a credential-less `main` checkout while treating release-PR content as untrusted API data, and confines write mutations to validated jobs using short-lived GitHub App tokens.
